decision: Car: stock Civic sedan FE (Zenki GLB v10, all Epsilon parts hidden) in Boost Blue Pearl; Epsilon parts shown in black
why: User asked for a bone-stock 11th-gen sedan. Boost Blue Pearl is the lookbook's paint for this car (the blue the user asked for on the EP3). Black parts are what the catalogue sells at the listed base price (unpainted PU lips and skirts, gloss-black wing) and they read clearly against the blue when applied.

decision: Cameras: one field of view for every view (f = 1757 px on 2560) and the pitch per view from the room's vanishing points; position from the game car's wheel contacts (menu view) or rear bumper (rear view) with El Camino dimensions; Civic stands on the game car's spot
why: No turntable or known car to solve against. Vertical + horizontal vanishing points agree on f within 1 % across menu, kit and rear views. Assumed wheelbase 2.95 m gives a 0.33 m tyre radius from the same picks, which is right for that car. First overlay put the Civic's wheels on the game car's.

decision: Menu re-lettered, not redrawn: Bodywork list = Front Lip / Sport Wing / Side Skirts / Rear Lip (row 2 = Sport Wing because that is the row the capture enters); Spoiler screen = Sport Wing, None 1/2 and Sport Wing $450 2/2; Full Kits = Epsilon Full Aero Kit with the four parts named; car tag = Honda / Jason's '22 Civic
why: Theme for our parts list while keeping the game's UI. Parts and the $450 are from Epsilon-Site showroom/catalog/products.json (Sport Wing, gloss black). No kit price is shown because the catalogue has none. Stat bars and their numbers are the game's own; on the kit screen the panel without the game kit's stat gains is used so no gain is implied for our kit. 'Not enough cash' and the $99 wallet are the capture's.

decision: Whips between views: capture's own 8 frames with the game car smeared along the pan, our car rendered from 8 orbit cameras interpolated between the two solved views
why: Each whip is 0.27 s of motion blur; solving it per frame is not worth it and the game car fills the frame there, so it cannot be covered. Keeps the capture's movement and timing.

decision: v1 timeline: menu (stock) 2.1 s > whip > Sport Wing screen, None 1.7 s > Sport Wing $450 2 s > whip back > menu, row moves to Side Skirts 2.7 s > Full Kits with the whole kit on 2.2 s > EPSILON+ card 2.5 s. 9:16 with the uncropped 16:9 frame on a blurred copy
why: Uses the capture's own actions and timing: enter a part, preview it, come back, then the full-kit screen as the payoff. The frame is not cropped because the game's menu uses the full width (list far left, stats far right). Sound is the capture's for the frames shown; menu ticks laid in at the three places the picture skips the capture's own.

decision: v2 story: the four parts are bought one after another and stay on: Front Lip and Side Skirts on the list screen (front view), cursor to Rear Lip, select, whip to the rear view, Rear Lip then Sport Wing there, whip back to the list with all four marked and the full kit on
why: User: the parts 'need to actually be combined with a confirmation sound effect'. The captures only have camera moves to the rear view, so the two front parts are fitted where they can be seen from the front camera and the two rear parts on the rear screen. Rows carry the game's yellow marker once fitted; the wallet starts at the four catalogue prices' total ($1,420) and pays for each ($1,135, $735, $450, $0) instead of the capture's $99 and 'Not enough cash'. The list calls the part Front Lip, which is what the catalogue sells for this car (user said front bumper).

decision: Confirmation = the game's own purchase from the second capture (3:33, the free kit): its 1.65 s sound at each install, the part appearing 0.1 s after the sound starts, 'Applied' with it, and the 'Purchased' pop-up 0.3 s later, cut out of that capture
why: User asked for a confirmation sound and then supplied a second capture to take audio and sounds from. The first capture never buys anything (its nearest sound is the 0.12 s select press). The second one buys once; timing of sound, state change and pop-up measured there (frames 12817, 12824-12830, 12836) and reused. Installs are spaced 1.8 s apart so the sound is not cut short.

decision: v3 order and views: list screen (Front Lip, Side Skirts) > Rear Lip on the second capture's Exhaust camera > Sport Wing on the first capture's rear camera > Respray on the first capture's option screen with the second capture's swatch block > Suspension and Rims on the second capture's own screens > UI-free shop frame (first capture, 68.1 s) with the mechanic's line as a subtitle > card
why: User's v2 brief, item by item. The exhaust angle was asked for by name for the rear lip. Menu-camera shots stay on the first capture (sunny, no uploader watermark); only angles it lacks come from the second, which carries the uploader's watermark bottom right. I left the watermark in: it is that creator's mark on their capture, and taking it off is the user's call, not mine.

decision: Car: Sonic Gray Pearl stock, parts paint-matched grey as they go on, respray to Boost Blue Pearl paints body and parts; lowered 45 mm; TE37-style 6-spoke 18s in bronze from the site's wheel set
why: User: parts paint matched, then a colour change that paints everything, then suspension and 'the custom wheels'. Grey to the lookbook blue makes the respray read. The site has two wheel models: the Civic Si factory wheel and the TE37-style one; only the second is a custom wheel. Bronze is my choice so the change shows against dark stock wheels. Drop amount is a look, not a product figure, and is not shown as a number.

decision: Prices and stats: Epsilon parts at catalogue prices; respray free, lowered suspension kit $750 and rims $560 are the game's own items, prices and stat changes, untouched; wallet starts at $2,730 and ends at $0
why: Never invent numbers. Epsilon sells no suspension or wheels, so those two screens keep the game's labels and figures (the +0.3 asphalt handling the user asked to see is the game's own number for its lowered kit). Rim name re-lettered to 'Custom 6-spoke rims' because the game's name described a different wheel.

decision: Mechanic's line: on-screen subtitle only, no voice
why: Neither capture contains the line (the first capture's exit line is a different one, and I cannot transcribe audio here: the speech model host is blocked). Generating a voice would spend the user's Higgsfield credits and pick a voice for their brand without asking; assemble3.py lays sfx/npc_line.wav at the line's frame if one is supplied.

decision: New cameras by hand (mancam.py): E -0.33 3.82 0.60 heading -82 pitch -5; S 2.737 -2.955 0.53 heading 128.7 pitch 0; W 2.089 -1.418 0.30 heading 185.3 pitch -1; f 1757 px
why: Heading from the vanishing point of the car's long axis in each view, distance from the tyre's radius on screen, position from where the front-left wheel (or the bumper) sits in the frame; overlays put the Civic's wheel on the game car's in S and W. E was then moved 0.6 m closer than the capture's exhaust camera so the narrower Civic covers the game car instead of leaving a third of the frame to invent.

decision: v4 audio: purchase sound rebuilt without the mechanic's voice (ticks 213.56-213.80 untouched, then only the chime's >4.5 kHz part plus the side channel below it); the line itself (second capture 213.80-215.45) plays once, at the exit, under its subtitle; room tone 9 dB lower with equal-power loop joins
why: User: 'the repeating need anything else is annoying, should only do it at the end'. The clip I had taken as the purchase sound carries the mechanic's line over the chime; I cannot hear, and had only looked at levels. Band analysis: bright stereo chime 213.9-214.7 s, centred speech-band sound from 213.8 s. A centred voice cancels in L-R (18 dB down where it is alone) and has nothing above 4.5 kHz in this capture. Not verified by ear.

decision: v4 no extra voice lines
why: User: vary the voice lines from the sample if there is an opportunity, never repeat one. Scanned both captures for dialogue subtitles (bottom-centre text every 0.25 s): the second capture shows only prompts, the first only its exit line over street noise. Without subtitles I cannot tell the mechanic's lines from other sounds, so only the one line the user identified is used, once. Asked the user for timestamps.

decision: v4 pricing and branding: parts priced as the catalogue's Sonic Gray Pearl (painted) variants: Front Lip $485, Side Skirts $800, Rear Lip $485, Sport Wing $850; EPSILON+ badge in the game's badge style and 'Epsilon ...' names on the list and each part screen; wallet starts at $3,930 and counts down over 0.4 s at each purchase to $0
why: User: 'add dynamic money/pricing so it is accurate - brand the kit as Epsilon'. v3 charged the unpainted prices for parts shown paint matched. The respray stays free and the suspension kit ($750) and rims ($560) keep the game's prices: Epsilon sells neither.

decision: v4 cameras: Front Lip on the second capture's front-bumper camera (F: 0 -4.12 0.95 heading 90 pitch -10), Side Skirts on its side camera (D: 3.283 -0.787 1.2 heading 152 pitch -6); the list screen is only the opening shot
why: User: 'the camera should snap to the front and sides for front lip and side skirts, like it does for rear lip and trunk wing'. Both moved in from the capture's positions so the Civic covers the game's car; the screens' own swatch blocks are masked and the part block is laid on as a layer.

decision: v4 wheel: 6-spoke wheel rebuilt from the original TE37 scan with the site's own generator at 160k triangles for the rim (was 8k) and the scanned tyre at 160k (was a plain revolved tyre); closing shot is a 150 degree camera orbit round the stationary finished car on black with the wordmark
why: User: 'improve the mesh of the 6 spoke custom wheels' and 'at the end have the camera pan around the car, car stationary, if possible'. The low-poly wheel was faceted in the wheel close-up. There is no 3D model of the shop, so an orbit inside the game scene is not possible; it is a studio render after the exit line.

decision: v5 brakes: when swapping wheels, the car's own brake disc and caliper are kept (old wheel stripped to its brake materials) and the wheel GLB's placeholder brake is hidden
why: User: 'fix the brake caliper underneath the 6 spoke wheels'. The TE37 wheel file carries a plain red block as a caliper and a featureless disc; the Civic model has a proper drilled disc and shaped caliper under its stock wheels. kit_render --wheels now does this for any showroom wheel.

decision: v5 side-skirt view: camera moved to 2.337 -1.077 1.1 (heading 152, pitch -8), 0.7 m closer and 0.7 m toward the nose, so the Civic covers 98 % of the game's car; the 3 % of frame left is filled by continuing the wall downward and mirroring the floor, with no blur
why: User: 'fix the environment blur so it is not as prominent on the side skirt camera change'. In v4 a third of the game's car stuck out behind the Civic and was replaced by a blurred column smear. Tried first: shift-map inpainting (smeared the car's orange across the frame), continuing the wall down over the whole gap (repeated the wall signs). Covering the gap with the car itself removes the problem instead of hiding it. Ten camera candidates scored by uncovered area; chose the one that still shows the rear wheel and the whole skirt.

decision: v6: closing orbit removed; reel ends on the in-shop exit shot with the mechanic's line, then the wordmark card. No in-garage 360.
why: User: skip the 360 if it cannot be rendered without bugging out; it was wanted in the environment, built from the longer video if needed. Tested: 782 frames at 2 fps from the longer capture give about 15 distinct camera positions (58 held views, most repeats with other paint); structure-from-motion (pycolmap, UI masked, per-image focal) registered 9 of 20 views into one model with 546 points and none of the views that look toward the front of the shop (rear, roof, engine). That is camera positions for half the room and no surfaces: a 360 would need the rest hand-built from flat frames with the game's car cut out of each, and racks, shelves and tool chests projected onto flat walls smear as the camera moves. Not clean, so skipped as instructed. Alternatives offered to the user: a walk-round of the finished car on the game's own cameras (front, side, rear, rear-high), or an AI-generated orbit from the final frame (their Higgsfield credits; the car's shape can drift).

decision: v7: list rows are plain part names (Front Lip, Side Skirts, Rear Lip, Sport Wing); the Epsilon name and EPSILON+ badge stay on each part's own screen
why: User: remove 'Epsilon' from the primary menu so it just says 'front lip' etc. Only the opening 46 frames were re-rendered (ONLY/OUTNAME in compose4.py) and spliced onto the v6 composite; frame count and alignment checked against v6.

decision: v8 side-skirt shot: low front-quarter camera (2.2 -1.9 0.55, heading 128.7, level) on the second capture's 'Wheel Kits' frames; skirt about 1,000 px long on screen between the two wheels; price block laid over the front wheel; background behind the tail mirrored in from the doorway. Suspension shot's background fill changed the same way.
why: User: 'point the camera down lower for the side skirt shot, the skirts don't fit in the frame'. Tilting the v5 side camera down needs 18 degrees from 2.3 m and leaves over 40 % of the frame as floor to invent; backing off from that side uncovers half the game's car. The low front-quarter view shows the sill naturally and the Civic covers 90 % of the game's car there. 18 positions scored by skirt length on screen and uncovered area. The camera is low and level rather than literally tilted down; told the user. It shares its angle with the suspension shot (closer here).

decision: v9 names: wing is 'Rear Wing' on the list, its screen title and its item name ('Epsilon Rear Wing'); suspension screen title back to the game's 'PRO BUILDS / WHEEL KITS'; 'COSMETICS / RESPRAY' and 'WHEELS / RIM STYLE' already matched the game
why: User: 'it should say rear wing instead of sport wing' and 'the menu title names should stay true to GTA 6'. Checked every title against the second capture: only 'Suspension' was mine. Part screens keep 'BODYWORK / <row name>', which is the game's own pattern (its row 'Spoiler' opens 'BODYWORK / SPOILER'), with the user's row names. The catalogue calls the part Sport Wing; the price is unchanged.

decision: v9 navigation: after the wing the reel returns to the Bodywork list (four rows marked), shoulder-tabs to COSMETICS (Respray, Customizable Liveries, Curated Liveries, Plates), selects Respray; after the respray back, tab to PRO BUILDS (Full Kits, Wheel Kits), down, select; after suspension back to the list, tab to WHEELS (Tire Style, Rim Style, Rim Colors), down, select. 3.7 s longer.
why: User: 'the menu skips the navigation to the paint section entirely'. Done for all three section changes, not only paint, so the menu logic is the same throughout. Rows read off the second capture at 29.6 s, 216.5 s and 346.5 s. Tab bar highlight moved on the first capture's frame (white box on the new tab, Bodywork redrawn unselected). Simplifications: one tab press shown from Pro Builds to Wheels (the game needs several), and the Wheels list is shown on the menu camera (the game moves to a wheel camera for that tab). Fitted entries carry the game's marker when the list is shown again.

decision: v10: suspension moved to the Performance tab: list Full Engine / Suspension / Brakes / Transmission / Boost, screen 'PERFORMANCE / SUSPENSION', item still the game's 'Lowered Suspension Kit' at $750; navigation Cosmetics > Bodywork > Performance (two tab presses), down one, select; then one press to Wheels
why: User: 'Wheel Kits is not suspension'. In v9 I restored the capture's own title for that screen (the game files its lowered kit under Pro Builds / Wheel Kits) after the user asked for titles true to GTA 6; that reads as a wheel menu to a viewer. Performance is where a suspension part belongs. The Suspension row is my addition to the game's four Performance rows; told the user. Only frames 469-632 re-rendered and spliced.

decision: v11 radio: the uploaded clip's audio from 2.0 s (where the song starts) laid as one unbroken 26.8 s bed from the reel's first frame to the cut to the card; band-limited 180 Hz-4.2 kHz, narrowed, short room tail; -33 dB RMS (purchase sounds -25, room tone -43); dips 4 dB under the mechanic's line; fades over its last 1.2 s
why: User: put this radio station in as in-game audio overlay, as background noise like the real game. One continuous piece because of the standing rule (never cut inside music). Processing is to make it sit in the room rather than on top of the mix. The clip is a screen recording of another creator's Short of the game's Honey FM (Buddy Guy, 'Stone Crazy', then the radio host): a commercial recording, and the creator may be audible on it; I cannot hear to check. Both told to the user.

decision: v12 navigation for the aero parts: each part is entered from the Bodywork list and left back to it (select, camera to the part, buy, back, camera to the list with the bought row marked, down one, select). Holds tightened so the menu is 26.2 s: part screens 2.0 s, respray 2.3 s, suspension and wheels 2.1 s, opening 1.0 s
why: User: 'the menu navigation for all the aero bits is also incorrect, it's skipping steps'. v4-v11 whipped from one part's camera straight to the next. Six more camera moves and three list beats add 2.6 s; trimmed elsewhere because the radio bed is 26.8 s long and must not be cut or looped.

decision: v12 watermark: on every frame from the second capture the bottom-right corner (x 1950-2560, y 1352-1436) is covered with mirrored floor from beside it and the first capture's clean 'BACK' hint is put back there
why: User: 'remove the watermark on the bottom right'. I had left it as the uploader's mark and said removing it was the user's call; they made it. The watermark also covered the game's own button hints (Rev / Buy / Back), so those go with it and one clean hint returns. Told the user again that it was that creator's credit.

decision: v13 end card: EPSILON+ wordmark (its own shape) filled with the GTA VI logo's vertical gradient, #445cc3 blue through #a241c0 purple and #fd6693 pink to #fe984a orange, purple edge #5a1f96, soft magenta glow, on black
why: User: finish with the Epsilon logo redone in GTA 6 colours. The ten gradient stops are medians sampled from the 'VI' in the GTA VI logo shown in the second capture (frame 110), not guessed. Only the palette is borrowed; the wordmark's letterforms are unchanged and nothing of Rockstar's logo is drawn.

decision: v14: car tag reads DINKA / JASON'S '22 BLISTA on every screen (was HONDA / JASON'S '22 CIVIC)
why: User: change '22 Civic to '22 Blista, in reference to the Dinka Blista (GTA's stand-in for the Civic). The maker line was changed to Dinka as well so the two lines agree; the user asked only for the model line, so this was flagged. The Honda badge on the car model itself is unchanged.

decision: v15: part screens re-sited so the Civic covers the game's car: front lip camera 0.4 m closer (0 -3.7 0.95), rear lip 0.4 m closer (-0.3 3.4 0.6), side skirts and suspension more head-on (2.0 -2.2 / -2.5, 0.55); front lip screen gets the stats panel and the pop-up above it like the other part screens
why: User: 'some of the purchased sections come out really poorly' and 'the front bumper is also missing the stats bar'. Looked at all seven purchase moments at delivery size: the pop-up itself is the game's and clean; what was poor was the invented background beside the car on the front lip (purple smear by the mirrors), rear lip (mirrored sign text) and side-skirt screens (smeared doorway), right where the pop-up appears. Uncovered game-car area is now 0-5 % on all of them (was 7-19 %).

decision: v15 respray: Recommended tab with the car's eleven factory colours as swatches; the cursor runs through all of them (3 frames and a tick each) with the car previewing each colour, stops on Boost Blue, which is bought. Exit shot is one frozen frame; list beats use forward frames only
why: User: 'change the colour swatch to Recommended and display all the OEM colours' and 'on the need-anything-else scene the car in the background is going back and forth constantly'. The game shows six swatches at a time, so running the cursor through the list is the game's own way of showing all eleven. Colours and finishes are the lookbook data for this car. The back-and-forth was my ping-pong loop of a ten-frame stretch of the capture, which reversed whatever moved outside the door.
